signature: MACHT HANNS HEINLEIN MDCXXXI NVR; maker's mark: cock’s head with initials “H H”; inspector's mark: stamp of Nuremberg inspection bureau (city coat of arms with "N"); owner's mark(?): Nuremberg coat of arms.
pitch: E-flat at a1 = 442 (Quint-bass); in D with tuning slide extended; intermediary piece can be removed, converting the instrument to a Sekund-posaune in A-flat (Kammerton).
mouthpiece: Boxwood, 2nd half of 17c / 1st half of 18c; diam. of bowl 18, bowl 6.5, outlet 7.2, depth of bowl 13.3, total length 93.3, width of rim 4.6; in former owner de Wit's time, this mouthpiece was associated with a tenor trombone made by Hanns Leonhard Ehe, Sr., D-L 1896.
dimensions: bo 11.3, be 122, le 4020 (in E-flat tuning), le 3112 (in A-flat tuning), int. diam. of mouthpipe 12.5.
remarks: 6 positions; bell at 4th pos. Flat slide stays have dragon-head hooks; hinged handle attached to moveable slide stay, probably added at a later date. Flat bell stay. Reverse taper in tuning slide. 2 coils of tubing in bell sec. when set up to play in E-flat. Two intermediate crooks, for F and G, probably belong to this instrument. Rings in slide-bow, bell-bow. Knob or ball in bell-pipe, like that of a trumpet. Tuning difficult to judge; sound is vigorous; when set up as a Sekund-posaune with wooden mp, loud, colorful; unattractive when set up as a Quint-bass.
